newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bonds staged a mild recovery in late trade on short-covering ahead of settlement on Thursday after a weak day as players continued to position themselves for the next stage in forex control relaxation on July 1.
The fixed income market had a shaky start, knocked by follow-through selling from Tuesday, when mainly jobbers cut long positions amid uncertainty ahead of the relaxation deadline.
Local institutions were seen holding to the fringes.
In addition, the technical picture had turned negative after a break through 14.74 percent on Tuesday, debt traders said, and the wobbly rand had not aided sentiment.
"It's all this uncertainty over July 1 that's causing the problem," one trader commented.
Another said there had been panic selling on Tuesday when the market breached key technical levels on the topside and most investors were uncertain about future direction, waiting for July 1 to pass.
"The perception is that the market will be better by year-end but the question is where is the entry point," a third noted.
He said local institutions had either been sidelined or sold small amounts while local traders and banks had sought value at the higher levels.
At 1430 GMT, government's R150 loan was yielding 14.83 percent from an intraday high of 14.88 percent and 14.80 percent in late Tuesday trade.
Since last Friday, long bonds have given up more than 25 basis points.

Dealers expected the debt market to move in a 10 point range on Thursday, around 14.81 to 14.89/14.90 percent amd most said a move beyond 15 percent was unlikely in the lead up to the forex control relaxation.
The move forms part of government plans to liberalise foreign exchange controls and will allow South African residents to invest offshore for the first time.
Financial markets fear that there will be an exodus of capital from the country.

The exact amount that individuals will be able to invest offshore has not yet been set but Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said recently that he expected the amount to be in the region of 160,000 rand per person.
Foreigners were net buyers of 105.00 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 21.18 million rands worth on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
The South African bond market was closed on Monday for the Youth Day holiday.
Nominal cumulative bond market volumes were at 6.2 billion rand from 4.8 billion rand on Friday.
The rand enjoyed a fair day, stabilising after a morning fall to a weakest bid of 4.5170 against the U.S. dollar.
At 1430 GMT it was at 4.5125/5155 to the dollar from 4.5085/5115 overnight.
"It was offshore dollar buying, local importer dollar buying and the weaker bond market," one forex trader said, describing the morning slide.
He said profit-taking and importer dollar demand was the order of the day as July 1 approached and a test of 4.5250 was on the cards by Friday.
Other traders said stop losses had been triggered on the way up at around 4.5000 and 4.4050 and there were more stop loss positions at 4.5250.
But the Reserve Bank was seen protecting that level and had acted to smooth out bumps and keep stability over the last few days.
"There's no panic at all and all moves are pretty orderly," one noted.
"He (the central bank) won't try stopping the move higher but he's there and the guys are scared of him".

Against the crosses, the rand was last at 25.0288/0676 against the yen from 25.1241/1630 on Tuesday, at 0.3821/3826 marks from 0.3840/3845 marks and at 7.3968/4062 against sterling from 7.3830/3925 previously.
On the money market, short-term rates were unchanged with three-month NCDs quoted at 16.05 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate also steady at between 15.45 to 15.60 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage fell to 7.324 billion rand on Tuesday from 7.610 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482-1003
